Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.

1. Heard Sri Shubham Yadav holding brief of Sri Bhola Singh Patel, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Ram Raj Singh, learned AGA for the State as well as Sri Pravin Kumar Verma,
Advocate, who has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party no. 2.
His Vakalatnama is taken on record.

2. This petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioners with the prayer to quash the chargesheet dated 30.05.2020 alongwith entire proceedings and summoning order dated 20.11.2020, on the basis of compromise, in Criminal Case No. 48038 of 2020 (State Vs. Sufiyan and others), arising out of Case Crime No. 684 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC, Section Sufiyan And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. District Lucknow, pending before the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-VII, Lucknow.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that earlier the petitioners approached this Court by means of Application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. No. 12649 of 2023, wherein this Court vide order dated 22.12.2023 directed the parties to file compromise deed before the concerned court below and the court below was directed to verify the contents and parties of the compromise deed.

4. In compliance of the aforesaid order, the compromise deed was filed before the court below and the court concerned vide report dated 06.01.2024 has verified the contents and parties of the compromise deed and submitted his report to the extent that the parties and contents of the compromise deed are genuine and they have entered into the compromise by free-will.
The report of the concerned court below dated 06.01.2024 is on record.
5. Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 has also submitted that the parties in dispute are not interested to pursue the criminal case.

6. The Apex Court in re: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343 has observed that even if the offence(s) in question is/are not compoundable within the scope of section 320 Cr.P.C. even then considering the facts and circumstances of the case in question the Constitutional Court may allow the parties to compound such offence(s) on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.
7.

entities.text: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Not only the above, considering the facts and circumstances of the issue in question and other dictums of Hon'ble Apex Court in re: B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; 2003 (4) SCC 675, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303; State of Rajasthan vs. Shambhu Kewat, (2014) 4 SCC 149; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Deepak (2014) 10 SCC 285; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Manish (2015) 8 SCC 307; J.Ramesh Kamath vs. Mohana Kurup (2016) 12 SCC 179;
State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Rajveer Singh (2016) 12 SCC 471; Parbatbhai AAhir vs. State of Gujarat (2017) 9 SCC 641 the entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case are hereby quashed.
